MRI RIGHT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Suspected meniscal tear.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
None

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: No evidence of meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Oblique tear of the posterior horn with extension to the inferior articular surface. No para meniscal cyst.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. No Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: No hyaline cartilage disease.

Medial compartment: No hyaline cartilage disease.

Lateral compartment: No hyaline cartilage disease.

Others:

Hoffa's fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Hairline non displaced oblique tear of the posterior horn of medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface.

No significant knee effusion. There is evidence of moderate diffuse thickening and edema of the PCL in keeping with a recent sprain. Normal ACL, MCL and LCL.  Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral and patellofemoral articular cartilage is normal. There is moderate diffuse marrow edema with mild microtrabecular fracturing within the anterior aspect of the tibial condyles.  
Conclusion:, PCL sprain. Anterior tibial contusion with microtrabecular fracturing.

MRI of Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, AX T2W FS, CO T2W FS



* There are linear signal intensity in the medial meniscus with extension into the surface, in favor of tear with medial displacement.
* Mild increased signal intensity in the anterior horn of lateral meniscus on F/S PD image, R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal, maybe due to myxoid degeneration or contusion.
* Articular cartilage wearing and osteophytes formation of right knee (including distal femur, proximal tibia and patella) with subchondral bone marrow edema over medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau, reflecting osteoarthritis with bone contusion.
* Small amount of joint effusion in right knee with suprapatellar extension, R/O synovitis.
* High signal in the soft tissues medial to the medial collateral ligament and medial patellar retinaculum, in favor of grade 1 injury.
* Increased fat stranding and some fluid accumulation located along the pes anserinus, R/O anserine bursitis.
> Some varicose veins in the medial aspect of right lower limb.
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> The lateral collateral ligament appears to be within normal.
> No significant muscle edema noted at distal thigh to proximal leg.

Impression:
1. C/W tear of medial meniscus with medial displacement.
2. R/O grade 2 intrasubstance signal in the anterior horn of lateral meniscus, maybe due to myxoid degeneration or contusion.
3. Osteoarthritis of right knee with osteophytes formation and subchondral bone marrow edema at the medial compartment and significant cartilage wearing/defect especially over medial side.
4. Few joint effusion and R/O synovitis and suprapatellar bursitis of right knee.
5. R/O pes anserine bursitis.
6. R/O grade 1 injury of medial collateral ligament and medial patellar retinaculum.

Suggest correlate with clinical manifestation.
